newsitem.title: UK: UK govt reviews commercial freedom for post office.
newsitem.headline: UK govt reviews commercial freedom for post office.

text.p: The Labour government on Friday announced it is launching a review of ways of giving the Post Office greater commercial freedom.

In its election manifesto, Labour said it was committed to giving the Post Office greater freedom while maintaining it in the public sector. The defeated Conservative government dropped plans to privatise the Post Office after public opposition.

Trade minister Ian McCartney said: "For too long now the Post Office, which is one of this country's major success stories, and an essential part of its social and commercial infrastructure, has been held back from developing its full potential both domestically and in the increasingly globalised international postal market place.
"We now intend to remove unnecessary and damaging shackles, whilst ensuring that competition between the Post Office and the private sector takes place on a fair and transparent basis."

McCartney said that in addition to discussions with the senior management of the Post Office, the government would also consult unions, users' groups and other interested parties -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
